newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST-Tight labor mkt a concern in US Jan jobs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Tight labor mkt a concern in US Jan jobs.

text.p: U.S. markets have discounted another healthy month of payrolls gains to begin 1997 but will be vulnerable to other fresh signs of labor market tightness when the Labor Department releases January employment figures.
The report is due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

With the economy already near full employment, economists said a solid advance in hourly earnings or a further decline in the jobless rate could change thinking at the Federal Reserve about the need for higher U.S. interest rates.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's veiled warnings about wage pressures in his recent testimony to the U.S. Senate have sensitized market participants to lingering tautness in the job market.

Although no change in interest rates occurred after the Fed's two-day policy meeting this week, the early reading on the central bank's intentions for late March will hinge in part on today's employment data.

"The thing that will be a catalyst for a Fed move over the next couple of months will be a further tightening of the labor market," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Inc.
"If the unemployment rate approaches five percent, even in the absence of any clear evidence of wage pressures, I think the Fed could step in and tighten."
Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the unemployment rate to dip to 5.2 percent in January after a reading of 5.3 percent in December.
They expect a healthy nonfarm payrolls advance of 237,000 after a sizable 262,000 climb in December.

The average workweek is expected to retreat to 34.6 hours after jumping to 34.8 in December. Growth in average hourly earnings is seen slowing to 0.2 percent after heady increases of 0.5 percent in December and 0.8 percent in November.
